subject.event: The article at https://example.com/article-8841 is predominantly machine-generated
subject.outcomeDefinition: Two of three independent human reviewers, working from the DID labelling rubric v2 and blind to the analyzer's output, label the article's body text as predominantly machine-generated.
subject.resolutionSource: DID labelled-corpus review panel; reviewers are external to the analyzer and do not see its scores.

interval.method: Bootstrap over the calibration corpus, 2000 resamples

baseline.source: Base rate in the labelled corpus
baseline.basis: Proportion of the 1,480-page labelled corpus judged predominantly machine-generated by the same panel process.

sampleSize.basis: The calibration corpus the score-to-probability mapping was fitted on, sampled across news, blog, and commerce domains.

outliers.handling: Nine corpus pages with contested labels (2-1 splits) were retained and carry the panel's disagreement; excluding them would have narrowed the mapping's uncertainty dishonestly.

regime.description: Generation models in wide use shifted materially since the corpus was labelled in 2025-11.
regime.accountedFor: The mapping's interval was widened by the observed drift between the 2025-11 and 2026-04 re-label subsets, and the confidence tier is capped at moderate until the corpus is refreshed.

market.reason: Nothing prices whether a specific page is machine-generated.

calibration.dataset: Held-out 20% of the 1,480-page labelled corpus, not used to fit the mapping.
